core: Foundations of legal interpretation, legal argument, jurisprudence and independent legal research
Public, constitutional, administrative and criminal law governing citizens and the state
Private, civil and commercial law governing persons, contracts and businesses
International, European and comparative legal order
adjacent: Business, finance and transnational commercial legal relationships
Legal philosophy, justice and social change
Public governance, taxation and policy institutions
questions: How do law and legal institutions balance public authority with private rights?
How do legal rules shape business transactions and public regulation?

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
trace: Definitions/legal systems and public/private fields, cases and trial simulations, followed by social/normative law-and-justice inquiry. Direct legal gateway with real skills, not the full Dutch foundational sequence.
Human-rights positive law, treaties, monitoring, case law, history and legal philosophy. Direct rights/justice inquiry, not professional legal ethics or a universal substitute for all jurisprudence.
Actual venture ideation, design thinking, market validation and business planning. Foundation for transnational business law, not incorporation or business-structure legal training.

Sources/subjects of public international law, force, armed conflict, international criminal/refugee/environmental law and treaty politics. Direct international legal substance, distinct from political IR.
Comparative constitutional and administrative principles across five legal systems, state powers, democracy and rights. Direct public-law substance; not deep Dutch administrative procedure.
Actual research design, sampling, statistics and a group project. Complementary empirical methods; no equivalence to positive-law research.
Qualitative research design, collection, analysis, positionality and group inquiry. Sound empirical complement retained in both schedules; it does not replace positive-law legal methods.

Criminal accountability, guilt, justifications, legality, punishment, reading legal texts/cases and simulated legal-aid clinic. Direct criminal legal substance; not the repeated Dutch procedure I/II sequence.
Political authority and legitimacy through classical/contemporary thinkers. Context for constitutional order, not the 13 EC Dutch/comparative constitutional-law course.
Social institutions, inequality and classical/colonial sociological theories. Social context for law, not a law-sociology specialisation.
Financial-statement and annual-report analysis/accounting practice. Genuine business context, not Dutch company-accounting law.

EU institutions/procedures, fundamental rights, citizenship, internal-market freedoms, research and PBL cases. Direct substantive/procedural EU legal study; not two full target EU units or Dutch litigation training.

Actual cross-border contracts, transactions, sales, intellectual property, investment, comparative law and arbitration simulation. Direct commercial legal substance, not Dutch company law or the full civil-law sequence.
Taxation, redistribution, spending, market failure and political economy. Policy/economic analysis of public revenue, not Dutch tax legislation.
Normative/practical ethics, moral responsibility and independent argumentative essay. Supports ethical reasoning, not the particular professional duties of Dutch lawyers.

Comparative property, contract, tort and private-law principles, primarily Germany/France/England/China/US. Direct private-law study; no Dutch civil I/II, tenancy, family or company-law specialisation inferred.
EU actors, decisions, interests and actual legislative-dossier group research. Political/institutional inquiry, not advanced European legal doctrine.
Civil society, public sphere, solidarity and NGO/CSO community research. Actual contemporary social theory, not historical development of private law.

Classical rhetoric, canons and types of argumentation, academic essay/oral presentation skills and rhetorical analysis. Self-contained writing/speaking contribution; no Dutch courtroom/procedure or legal-research qualification.
Violence, structural/identity/colonial causes and peacebuilding. Societal conflict inquiry, not criminal procedure or crime-law doctrine.
Movement theories and Environmental Justice Atlas cases, feminism, anticolonialism and environmental peacebuilding. Societal justice context, not environmental litigation.
IR theories, geopolitics, international institutions and Security Council simulation. Institutional context, not public international law by itself.
Rule-making actors, interests, public opinion and policy enforcement through concrete sustainability cases. Genuine governance study, not environmental legal doctrine or administrative procedure.
Actual micro/macro foundations, game theory, consumer/firm behaviour, output, inflation and financial markets. Economic context for legal institutions, not legal doctrine.
Consumer behaviour, uncertainty, imperfect competition, factor markets, welfare and externalities. Economic analysis, not a dedicated contract-law or financial-law course.
Institutional, political and cultural global-business governance, responsibility, geopolitics and trade. Business context, not Dutch company-law doctrine.
OLS/GLS/IV, tests, Monte Carlo/Stata and an empirical paper. Advanced empirical inquiry, not statutory/case-law methodology or a Dutch legal thesis.
Actual financial-data analysis, risk, investment, budgeting and business decisions. No specialist banking or financial-regulation content is established by the title.

alternatives.label: Law, public institutions and society
alternatives.concept: A related UCR programme with 60 EC of direct legal study: legal systems, human rights, comparative constitutional/administrative law, criminal law, public international law, EU law, comparative private law and transnational business law. Political institutions, sociology, justice, rhetoric and empirical inquiry add context. It does not reproduce the cumulative Dutch doctrinal, procedural, legal-history, moot-court and thesis requirements.
alternatives.labelReason: Actual public/criminal/constitutional/international/EU/private law is combined with political and social institutions; the label signals a related broad legal response.
progression: All actual assigned-term offerings and formal prerequisites checked; rhetoric is self-contained, and no advanced persuasion course with assumed rhetorical background is scheduled. PPD is in Year 1.

alternatives.label: Law, business and economic institutions
alternatives.concept: A related programme retains the same 60 EC legal core while adding economic theory, financial-statement analysis, empirical economic research, financial decisions and global-business institutions. Its business and economics content supports analysis of legal and commercial settings; it is not Dutch company, banking, tax or financial-reporting law.
alternatives.labelReason: Five courses change to a sustained business/economic lens; broader law remains explicit, and the title does not promise a specialist Dutch private-law degree.
progression: All actual prerequisites and offerings checked; business foundation precedes transnational business law/global business/finance, methods precedes advanced economics, and self-contained rhetoric replaces advanced persuasion.
alternatives.distinctness: Exactly five different courses per programme,37.5EC. The main has political philosophy,EU politics,peace/conflict,social movements and sustainability governance; this route has introductory economics,microeconomics,international business governance,econometrics andfinancialdecisionmaking. Same19courses/shared142.5EC; real contextual and methodological change, not a new specialist-law claim.

General moral theory and practical ethical argument support normative reasoning; professional duties of Dutch lawyers remain distinct.
Property, contract and tort principles provide real private-law study through a comparative approach rather than Dutch civil-law coverage.

notes.text: UCR provides 60 EC of direct legal study across comparative public and private law, criminal law, international and EU law, human rights and transnational business law. Radboud has a much denser Dutch doctrinal and procedural sequence, legal history, simulated court work and a legal thesis. The UCR programmes offer related study without reproducing this full legal degree or establishing civiel effect, professional qualification or master admission.

audience.programmeDescription: Law at Radboud studies public and private legal relationships, criminal justice, international and European law, and the historical and philosophical foundations of law. It develops legal interpretation and research through a cumulative Dutch-law curriculum, simulated courts and a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Two related UCR programmes share 60 EC of direct legal study. One adds public institutions, society and justice; the other adds business, economics and financial analysis. Both develop real legal knowledge while remaining broader than Radboud’s Dutch doctrinal, procedural, legal-history and thesis sequence.

curriculum.limitation: The complete 180 EC comprises 162 EC of compulsory study and 18 EC of restricted choices: Labour Law, Tenancy Law, AI and Law, and a linked Criminology perspective and essay are selected here. Other permitted choices are alternatives. There is no open elective block or reserved exchange semester. Tutoring participation is required without extra credit. The five-credit thesis has academic-skills entry requirements; active first-year participation and progression rules apply. UCR programmes do not establish Dutch legal professional qualification, civiel effect or master admission.
